questions.stem: Two complementary angles measure $x^\circ$ and $2x^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add up to $90^\circ$, so $x + 2x = 90$. Then $3x = 90$ and $x = 30$.

questions.skill: Solving for an unknown angle with an equation
questions.stem: Two supplementary angles measure $x^\circ$ and $(x + 40)^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add to $180^\circ$: $x + (x + 40) = 180$, so $2x + 40 = 180$ and $2x = 140$. Then $x = 70$.

questions.skill: Writing an equation for an angle relationship
questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. One measures $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and the other measures $50^\circ$. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$, so the sum of the two measures is 180: $(2x + 10) + 50 = 180$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle measures $(3x + 5)^\circ$ and the angle vertical to it measures $65^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so $3x + 5 = 65$. Then $3x = 60$ and $x = 20$.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles on a line
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One of the angles formed measures $112^\circ$. What is the measure of an angle adjacent to it, in degrees?
questions.solution: Adjacent angles formed by two crossing lines lie along a straight line, so they add to $180^\circ$. $180 - 112 = 68$ degrees.

solve.work: Adjacent angles at crossing lines form a linear pair: 180 - 112 = 68.

questions.skill: Naming angle relationships
questions.stem: Two angles measure $35^\circ$ and $55^\circ$. Which statement is true?
choices: The angles are vertical, because both are less than $90^\circ$
questions.solution: The sum is $35 + 55 = 90$, so the angles are complementary. Supplementary angles would add to 180.

questions.skill: Solving for an unknown angle with an equation
questions.stem: An angle's complement is $20^\circ$ more than the angle itself. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its complement is $x + 20$, and they add to 90: $2x + 20 = 90$, so $x = 35$. The complement is $55^\circ$.

solve.work: Angle a, complement 90 - a = a + 20, so 2a = 70, a = 35. Check: complement 55 = 35 + 20.

questions.skill: Solving for an unknown angle with an equation
questions.stem: An angle's supplement is 3 times as large as the angle. What is the measure of the angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its supplement is $3x$, and they add to $180^\circ$. So $4x = 180$ and $x = 45$.

questions.skill: Reasoning about angle pairs
questions.stem: Angles 1 and 2 are vertical angles. Angles 2 and 3 are adjacent angles on a straight line. Angle 1 measures $50^\circ$. What does angle 3 measure?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so angle 2 measures $50^\circ$. Angle 3 and angle 2 add to $180^\circ$, so angle 3 is $180 - 50 = 130^\circ$.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles on a line
questions.stem: Three adjacent angles lie along a straight line. Two of them measure $30^\circ$ and $100^\circ$, and the third measures $x^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: The three angles together make a straight line, $180^\circ$. $30 + 100 + x = 180$, so $x = 180 - 130 = 50$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles
questions.stem: Two lines cross. Two vertical angles measure $(5x - 20)^\circ$ and $(3x + 10)^\circ$. What is the measure of each of these angles?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal: $5x - 20 = 3x + 10$, so $2x = 30$ and $x = 15$. Each angle is $3(15) + 10 = 55^\circ$.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles on a line
questions.stem: Two lines cross. Two adjacent angles measure $(4x + 8)^\circ$ and $(2x + 22)^\circ$. What is the measure of the larger of the two angles, in degrees?
questions.solution: Adjacent angles from crossing lines add to $180^\circ$: $6x + 30 = 180$, so $x = 25$. The angles are $4(25) + 8 = 108$ and $2(25) + 22 = 72$. The larger is 108 degrees.

solve.work: Linear pair: 4x + 8 + 2x + 22 = 180, 6x = 150, x = 25. Angles 108 and 72; larger 108.

questions.skill: Writing an equation for an angle relationship
questions.stem: Two angles are complementary. One is $12^\circ$ less than twice the other. If the smaller angle is $x$, which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: The other angle is twice $x$ minus 12, which is $2x - 12$. Complementary angles add to 90, so $x + (2x - 12) = 90$.

solve.work: Smaller x, other 2x - 12; complementary: x + (2x - 12) = 90 (x = 34, other 56, so x is indeed smaller).

questions.skill: Solving for an unknown angle with an equation
questions.stem: An angle measures $15^\circ$ more than 2 times its complement. What is the measure of the angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its complement is $90 - x$. So $x = 2(90 - x) + 15$, which gives $x = 195 - 2x$. Then $3x = 195$ and $x = 65$. Its complement is $25^\circ$ and $2(25) + 15 = 65$.

questions.skill: Solving for an unknown angle with an equation
questions.stem: Two angles are complementary. One measures $(4x + 6)^\circ$ and the other measures $(2x - 12)^\circ$. What is the measure of the smaller angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: The sum is 90: $(4x + 6) + (2x - 12) = 90$, so $6x - 6 = 90$ and $x = 16$. The angles are $4(16) + 6 = 70$ and $2(16) - 12 = 20$. The smaller is 20 degrees.

questions.skill: Reasoning about angle pairs
questions.stem: Angles 1 and 2 are complementary. Angles 2 and 3 are supplementary. Angle 1 measures $28^\circ$. What does angle 3 measure?
questions.solution: Angle 2 is $90 - 28 = 62^\circ$. Angle 3 is supplementary to angle 2, so it measures $180 - 62 = 118^\circ$.

questions.skill: Reasoning about angle pairs
questions.stem: Two lines cross. Two adjacent angles measure $(x + 30)^\circ$ and $(2x + 60)^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle vertical to the larger of these two angles?
questions.solution: Adjacent angles add to 180: $3x + 90 = 180$, so $x = 30$. The angles are $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$. The larger is $120^\circ$, and its vertical angle is equal to it.

solve.work: Linear pair: x + 30 + 2x + 60 = 180, 3x = 90, x = 30. Angles 60 and 120. Vertical to larger = 120.

questions.skill: Solving for an unknown angle with an equation
questions.stem: A ray splits a straight angle into two angles whose measures are in the ratio 2 to 3. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
questions.solution: Let the angles be $2x$ and $3x$. They add to $180^\circ$: $5x = 180$ and $x = 36$. The smaller angle is $2(36) = 72^\circ$.

questions.skill: Reasoning about angle pairs
questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. Which statement must be true?
choices: Both angles are acute angles of equal measure
The two angles share a side
If one is obtuse, then the other is acute
questions.answer: If one is obtuse, then the other is acute
questions.solution: An obtuse angle is more than $90^\circ$, so the other angle is less than $180 - 90 = 90^\circ$, which makes it acute. The other statements need not be true.

solve.answer: If one is obtuse, then the other is acute
solve.work: Sum 180: if one > 90 the other < 90, so acute. Others need not hold (need not share a side; e.g. 100 and 80).

questions.skill: Angles on a straight line in an equation
questions.stem: Two rays from the same point on a straight line split the straight angle into three angles that measure $x^\circ$, $2x^\circ$ and $(x + 40)^\circ$. What is the measure of the largest of the three angles, in degrees?
questions.solution: The three angles together make a straight angle: $x + 2x + (x + 40) = 180$. Then $4x + 40 = 180$, so $4x = 140$ and $x = 35$. The angles are $35^\circ$, $70^\circ$ and $75^\circ$, so the largest is $75^\circ$.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: A figure is made of two rectangles joined side by side. One is 6 centimeters by 4 centimeters and the other is 3 centimeters by 4 centimeters. What is the area of the whole figure in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has area $6 \times 4 = 24$ and the second has area $3 \times 4 = 12$. The whole figure has area $24 + 12 = 36$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism
questions.stem: A box shaped like a rectangular prism is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 3 inches tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $8 \times 5 \times 3 = 120$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Volume of a pyramid
questions.stem: A pyramid has a base with an area of 18 square centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is its volume?
questions.solution: The volume of a pyramid is one third of the base area times the height: $\frac{1}{3} \times 18 \times 5 = 30$ cubic centimeters. Leaving out the one third gives 90.

questions.skill: Surface area of a prism
questions.stem: A cube has edges that are each 5 centimeters long. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 faces, each a square of area $5 \times 5 = 25$. The surface area is $6 \times 25 = 150$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: A square 10 meters on each side has a square 3 meters on each side cut out of one corner. What is the area of the figure that is left?
questions.solution: The big square has area $10 \times 10 = 100$ and the piece cut out has area $3 \times 3 = 9$. What is left has area $100 - 9 = 91$ square meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a composite figure
questions.stem: Two squares with sides of 5 centimeters are joined along a full side to make a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the rectangle in centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 10 centimeters long and 5 centimeters wide. Its perimeter is $10 + 5 + 10 + 5 = 30$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a square base 4 centimeters on each side. Each of its 4 triangular faces has an area of 10 square centimeters. What is the surface area of the pyramid?
questions.solution: The base has area $4 \times 4 = 16$ and the four triangles have area $4 \times 10 = 40$. The surface area is $16 + 40 = 56$ square centimeters. The answer 40 leaves out the base.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: A house-shaped figure is a rectangle 6 meters wide and 4 meters tall with a triangle on top. The triangle has a base of 6 meters and a height of 2 meters. What is the area of the whole figure in square meters?
questions.solution: The rectangle has area $6 \times 4 = 24$. The triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 2 = 6$. The whole figure has area $24 + 6 = 30$ square meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a composite figure
questions.stem: A rectangle 4 centimeters long and 3 centimeters wide is joined to a square with 3-centimeter sides, along a 3-centimeter side, to make one larger rectangle. What is the perimeter of the larger rectangle?
questions.solution: The larger rectangle is $4 + 3 = 7$ centimeters long and 3 centimeters wide. Its perimeter is $7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20$ centimeters. Adding the two separate perimeters gives 26, which counts the joined side twice.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has a triangular base with a base of 6 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters. The prism is 10 centimeters long. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ square centimeters. The volume is the base area times the length: $12 \times 10 = 120$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: A rectangle 12 meters by 9 meters has a rectangle 5 meters by 4 meters cut out of one corner. What is the area of the figure that is left, in square meters?
questions.solution: The large rectangle has area $12 \times 9 = 108$. The piece cut out has area $5 \times 4 = 20$. What is left has area $108 - 20 = 88$ square meters.

questions.skill: Volume of a pyramid
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base 6 centimeters on each side and a height of 9 centimeters. What is its volume?
questions.solution: The base area is $6 \times 6 = 36$ square centimeters. The volume is $\frac{1}{3} \times 36 \times 9 = 108$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a prism
questions.stem: A box is 10 inches long, 6 inches wide, and 4 inches tall. What is its surface area in square inches?
questions.solution: The faces come in three pairs: $10 \times 6 = 60$, $10 \times 4 = 40$ and $6 \times 4 = 24$. Doubling the sum gives $2 \times (60 + 40 + 24) = 248$ square inches.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a composite figure
questions.stem: An L-shaped figure has only right angles. Going around it, its sides measure 10, 3, 6, 5, 4 and 8 centimeters. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: The perimeter is the sum of all the sides: $10 + 3 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 8 = 36$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism
questions.stem: A prism has a base that is a right triangle with legs of 6 centimeters and 8 centimeters. The prism is 10 centimeters tall. What is its volume?
questions.solution: The base has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24$ square centimeters. The volume is $24 \times 10 = 240$ cubic centimeters. Forgetting the one half gives 480.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a square base 10 centimeters on each side. Each of its four triangular faces has a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 8 centimeters. What is the surface area of the pyramid in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The base has area $10 \times 10 = 100$. Each triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 8 = 40$, so the four have area 160. The total is $100 + 160 = 260$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: A figure is a rectangle 12 centimeters long and 8 centimeters wide with a triangle attached along one 8-centimeter side. The triangle has a base of 8 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is the area of the whole figure in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle has area $12 \times 8 = 96$. The triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20$. Together: $96 + 20 = 116$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a prism
questions.stem: A box with no lid is 8 centimeters long, 5 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. How many square centimeters of cardboard cover its outside (the bottom and four sides)?
questions.solution: The bottom is $8 \times 5 = 40$. The two long sides are $8 \times 3 = 24$ each and the two short sides are $5 \times 3 = 15$ each, so the sides total $48 + 30 = 78$. Altogether $40 + 78 = 118$. A closed box would have 158, and 120 is the volume.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a composite figure
questions.stem: A rectangle 10 meters long and 6 meters wide has a 3-meter by 2-meter rectangle cut out of one corner. What is the perimeter of the figure that is left, in meters?
questions.solution: Cutting a corner rectangle takes away 3 meters and 2 meters from the boundary but adds the same 3 meters and 2 meters along the cut. The perimeter stays that of the original rectangle: $2 \times (10 + 6) = 32$ meters.

solve.work: Cutting a corner rectangle leaves perimeter unchanged: 2(10+6) = 32.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A block is 5 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. A square hole 2 centimeters by 2 centimeters goes straight through its 3-centimeter height. What is the volume of the block with the hole?
questions.solution: The whole block has volume $5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60$. The hole removes $2 \times 2 \times 3 = 12$. What is left has volume $60 - 12 = 48$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: An L-shaped figure has only right angles. Going around it, its sides measure 12, 4, 7, 5, 5 and 9 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Think of the L as a 12 by 9 rectangle with a 7 by 5 piece cut out of one corner. The area is $12 \times 9 - 7 \times 5 = 108 - 35 = 73$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has triangular ends with sides of 3, 4 and 5 centimeters (a right triangle with legs 3 and 4). The prism is 10 centimeters long. What is its surface area?
questions.solution: Each triangular end has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = 6$, so the two ends have area 12. The three rectangles have a combined width of $3 + 4 + 5 = 12$ and length 10, so area 120. The total is $12 + 120 = 132$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a pyramid
questions.stem: A pyramid has a volume of 40 cubic centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. What is the area of its base in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The volume is $\frac{1}{3} \times B \times 6 = 2B$, so $2B = 40$ and the base area is $B = 20$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A solid is a rectangular prism 6 centimeters by 4 centimeters by 5 centimeters with a pyramid on top. The pyramid has the same 6 by 4 base and a height of 6 centimeters. What is the volume of the solid?
questions.solution: The prism has volume $6 \times 4 \times 5 = 120$. The pyramid has volume $\frac{1}{3} \times 24 \times 6 = 48$. Together: $120 + 48 = 168$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid
questions.stem: A rectangular pyramid has a base 18 centimeters by 10 centimeters. Two of its triangular faces each have a base of 18 centimeters and a height of 13 centimeters. The other two each have a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 15 centimeters. What is its surface area?
questions.solution: The base has area $18 \times 10 = 180$. The first two triangles have area $\frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 13 = 117$ each, and the other two have area $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 15 = 75$ each. The total is $180 + 234 + 150 = 564$ square centimeters. The answer 384 leaves out the base.

solve.work: Base 180; 2 x (1/2)(18)(13) = 234; 2 x (1/2)(10)(15) = 150; total 564. Consistent: height 12 gives slants 13 and 15.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a composite figure
questions.stem: A house-shaped figure has a flat bottom of 6 meters, two vertical sides of 4 meters each, and two sloping roof sides of 5 meters each. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: The perimeter is the distance around the outside: $6 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 5 = 24$ meters. The 30 would also count a line across the bottom of the roof, which is not on the boundary.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has a volume of 180 cubic centimeters. Its triangular base has a base of 9 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. How many centimeters long is the prism?
questions.solution: The triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 5 = 22.5$ square centimeters. Since volume is base area times length, the length is $180 \div 22.5 = 8$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a pyramid
questions.stem: A pyramid has a rectangular base 7 centimeters by 6 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters. What is its volume?
questions.solution: The base area is $7 \times 6 = 42$ square centimeters. The volume is $\frac{1}{3} \times 42 \times 10 = 140$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a prism
questions.stem: A tent is a triangular prism. Each triangular end has sides of 5, 5 and 6 meters and an area of 12 square meters. The tent is 10 meters long. The two ends and the three rectangular sides (the floor and two slanted sides) are all made of canvas. How many square meters of canvas are needed?
questions.solution: The two triangular ends have area $2 \times 12 = 24$. The three rectangles are each 10 meters long with widths 5, 5 and 6, so their area is $(5 + 5 + 6) \times 10 = 160$. The total is $24 + 160 = 184$ square meters.

solve.work: Ends 2 x 12 = 24; rectangles (5+5+6) x 10 = 160; total 184. Triangle 5,5,6 has height 4, area 12, consistent.

questions.skill: Area of a composite figure
questions.stem: A square garden is 14 meters on each side. In it are a rectangular pond 6 meters by 4 meters and a triangular flower bed with a base of 8 meters and a height of 5 meters. What is the area of the garden that is not pond or flower bed, in square meters?
questions.solution: The garden has area $14 \times 14 = 196$. The pond has area $6 \times 4 = 24$ and the flower bed has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20$. What is left is $196 - 24 - 20 = 152$ square meters.

questions.skill: Tell the population from the sample
questions.stem: A school has 800 students. The principal surveys 40 of them about school lunch. What is the population?
choices: The lunch food the school serves
questions.solution: The population is the whole group we want to learn about, which is all 800 students. The 40 students surveyed are only the sample.

solve.work: The population is the whole group of interest: all 800 students; the 40 are the sample.

questions.skill: Tell the population from the sample
questions.stem: A factory makes 1,000 light bulbs in a day and tests 25 of them. How many bulbs are in the sample?
questions.solution: The sample is the part of the group that is actually tested. Here 25 bulbs are tested, so the sample has 25 bulbs. (The population is all 1,000 bulbs.)

solve.work: The sample is the bulbs actually tested: 25.

questions.skill: Choose a random, representative sampling method
questions.stem: A school wants to know which sport its students like best. Which would give a random sample?
choices: Ask the 30 students who happen to be standing in the gym
Pick 30 names from a hat holding all students' names
Ask the 30 students who play on the school football team
Ask 30 friends of the person doing the survey
questions.answer: Pick 30 names from a hat holding all students' names
questions.solution: In a random sample, every student has an equal chance of being picked. Drawing names from a hat does that. The other groups are chosen because of where they are or who they know, so they are not random.

solve.answer: Pick 30 names from a hat holding all students' names
solve.work: Drawing names from a hat of all students gives each an equal chance; the others are convenience/biased groups.

questions.skill: Spot why a sample is biased
questions.stem: Mina wants to know the favorite pet of the students in her school. She asks only students in the pet club. Why might this sample not represent the whole school?
choices: Pet club members are not typical of the school
Too many students in the school were asked this question
The students were picked by a fair random drawing
Students cannot be asked about their favorite pets
questions.answer: Pet club members are not typical of the school
questions.solution: Pet club members may feel differently about pets than other students, so the sample leaves out the views of many. A sample should be a fair picture of the whole group.

solve.answer: Pet club members are not typical of the school
solve.work: Pet club members likely like pets/particular pets more than typical students, so the sample is biased.

questions.skill: Sample size
questions.stem: A school has 2,000 students. Which random sample would best represent the whole school?
choices: A random sample of ten students
A random sample of two students
questions.solution: A larger random sample is more likely to be close to the whole population. 200 is the largest of these samples.

solve.work: Larger random samples give more reliable estimates; 200 is the largest.

questions.skill: Use a sample to estimate for the population
questions.stem: A random sample of 10 students from a class of 30 shows that 4 of the 10 like soccer. Based on the sample, how many of the 30 students would you predict like soccer?
questions.solution: 4 out of 10 is $\frac{4}{10}$ of the sample. Apply that share to the class of 30: $\frac{4}{10} \cdot 30 = 12$.

questions.skill: Judge whether a generalization is valid
questions.stem: In a random sample of 10 students from a school, 8 say they like pizza. Which statement is reasonable for all the students at the school?
choices: Every student at the school likes pizza
No student at the school dislikes pizza
Exactly 8 students at the school like pizza
Most of the students probably like pizza
questions.answer: Most of the students probably like pizza
questions.solution: The sample is random, so it is a fair picture of the school. Since 8 of 10 like pizza, most students probably do. A sample cannot tell us that every student does, or give exact counts.

solve.answer: Most of the students probably like pizza
solve.work: 8/10 = 80% in a random sample suggests most students probably like pizza; certainty claims are not valid.

questions.skill: Choose a random, representative sampling method
questions.stem: A store has a list of 500 customers. Which is the best way to choose 20 customers at random?
choices: Take the first 20 names that appear on the list
Use a random number picker to choose 20 names
Pick 20 people who look friendly and helpful
Choose the 20 customers who spent the most money
questions.answer: Use a random number picker to choose 20 names
questions.solution: A random number picker gives every customer the same chance of being chosen. Using the first names, friendly people or big spenders favors certain customers.

solve.answer: Use a random number picker to choose 20 names
solve.work: A random number picker gives every customer an equal chance.

questions.skill: Spot why a sample is biased
questions.stem: Lee wants to know which sport the people in his town like best. He asks only people leaving a football game. Why might the answers mislead him?
choices: They may like football more than most people do
The people he asked were all too tired to answer
He asked about sports instead of about games
A football game does not have enough people
questions.answer: They may like football more than most people do
questions.solution: People who go to a football game are more likely than most to name football as their favorite. His sample favors one answer, so it does not represent the town.

solve.answer: They may like football more than most people do
solve.work: People leaving a football game likely favour football more than the town in general: biased sample.

questions.skill: Tell the population from the sample
questions.stem: A newspaper polls 300 of the 12,000 voters in a town. How many voters are in the population?
questions.solution: The population is every voter the poll is meant to describe, which is all 12,000 voters. The 300 people polled are the sample.

questions.skill: Tell the population from the sample
questions.stem: A company has 3,000 employees. Which is a sample of its employees?
choices: All 3,000 employees who work at the company
Every employee on the payroll of the company
The 150 employees picked by drawing names
The complete list of all 3,000 employee names
questions.answer: The 150 employees picked by drawing names
questions.solution: A sample is a part of the population. 150 employees picked from the 3,000 is a part. The other choices all describe the whole company.

solve.answer: The 150 employees picked by drawing names
solve.work: A sample is a subset: the 150 drawn employees.

questions.skill: Choose a random, representative sampling method
questions.stem: A city wants to know how residents feel about a new bus route. Which is the best way to choose the sample?
choices: Survey 400 people who are waiting at the bus station
Survey 400 people who live along the new bus route
Survey the first 400 people who answer an online post
Randomly choose 400 homes from a list of all homes
questions.answer: Randomly choose 400 homes from a list of all homes
questions.solution: Choosing addresses at random gives every resident a chance to be included. People at the bus station, along the route, or who answer an online post are not typical of all residents.

solve.answer: Randomly choose 400 homes from a list of all homes
solve.work: Random choice from a list of all homes gives every household a chance; others are self-selected or biased by location/use.

questions.skill: Spot why a sample is biased
questions.stem: A radio station asks listeners to call in and say whether they like country music. Why might the results mislead about all people in the town?
choices: Too many people live in the town to be surveyed
Callers pick themselves, so they may differ from the town
Radio stations are not allowed to ask listeners questions
Callers always give wrong answers to the questions
questions.answer: Callers pick themselves, so they may differ from the town
questions.solution: When people choose for themselves whether to respond, the ones who respond may feel differently from the rest. A random sample would avoid this.

solve.answer: Callers pick themselves, so they may differ from the town
solve.work: Call-in is voluntary response; callers self-select and may differ from the town.

questions.skill: Sample size
questions.stem: Sam surveys a random sample of 15 students and Lia surveys a random sample of 150 students from the same school. Whose result is more likely to be close to what the whole school thinks?
choices: Lia's, because a larger random sample is usually closer
Sam's, because a smaller random sample is more accurate
Sam's, because a small group is easier to ask questions
Neither, because random samples are never very close
questions.answer: Lia's, because a larger random sample is usually closer
questions.solution: Both samples are random, but the larger one has less chance of being far from the population. Lia's sample of 150 is more likely to be close.

solve.answer: Lia's, because a larger random sample is usually closer
solve.work: Larger random samples tend to be closer to the population value: Lia's 150.

questions.skill: Use a sample to estimate for the population
questions.stem: A random sample of 80 students from a school of 1,200 shows that 20 students ride the bus. Based on the sample, how many of the 1,200 students would you predict ride the bus?
questions.solution: 20 out of 80 is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the sample. A quarter of 1,200 is $1200 \div 4 = 300$.

questions.skill: Use a sample to estimate for the population
questions.stem: In a random sample of 50 phones from a day's production of 2,000 phones, 3 are faulty. Based on the sample, how many of the 2,000 phones would you predict are faulty?
questions.solution: 3 out of 50 is $\frac{3}{50}$. Of 2,000 phones, $\frac{3}{50} \cdot 2000 = 120$.

questions.skill: Judge whether a generalization is valid
questions.stem: A random sample of 100 voters in a town of 20,000 shows that 62 favor a new library. Which is the most reasonable conclusion?
choices: Exactly 62 percent of all the town's voters favor it
Every voter in the town favors building the library
More than half of the voters probably favor it
Only 62 voters in the whole town favor the library
questions.answer: More than half of the voters probably favor it
questions.solution: The sample is random, so its result is close to the truth, but not exact. 62 of 100 is more than half, so more than half of all voters probably favor the library.

solve.answer: More than half of the voters probably favor it
solve.work: 62% in a random sample of 100 suggests probably more than half favour it; 'exactly 62%' overclaims.

questions.skill: Judge whether a generalization is valid
questions.stem: A survey of the 30 players on a school's basketball team finds that all of them like basketball. Which conclusion about all students is valid?
choices: All students at the school like basketball
Most students at the school like basketball
Half of the students at the school like basketball
This group cannot tell us about all students
questions.answer: This group cannot tell us about all students
questions.solution: The team members were not chosen at random and are likely to like basketball more than other students. No valid conclusion about all students can be drawn from them.

solve.answer: This group cannot tell us about all students
solve.work: Basketball team players are not representative of all students; no valid conclusion about the school.

questions.skill: Choose a random, representative sampling method
questions.stem: A principal numbers the 600 students from 1 to 600 and wants a random sample of 30. Which method gives a random sample?
choices: Pick the numbers 1 through 30 on the list
Have a computer pick 30 numbers at random
Pick the 30 students with the highest grades
Pick the 30 students who are the tallest
questions.answer: Have a computer pick 30 numbers at random
questions.solution: A random number generator gives each student the same chance. The numbers 1 through 30 are a fixed group, and grades and height are not random.

solve.answer: Have a computer pick 30 numbers at random
solve.work: A computer choosing 30 numbers at random gives each student an equal chance.

questions.skill: Sample size
questions.stem: A school with 840 students wants a random sample of 10 percent of its students. How many students should be in the sample?
questions.solution: 10 percent of 840 is $840 \div 10 = 84$ students.

questions.skill: Use a sample to estimate for the population
questions.stem: A random sample of 150 students in a county shows that 54 of them ride the bus. The county has 8,500 students. Based on the sample, how many students in the county would you predict ride the bus?
questions.solution: 54 out of 150 is $\frac{54}{150} = 0.36$ of the sample. Apply that share to 8,500 students: $0.36 \cdot 8500 = 3060$.

questions.skill: Judge whether a generalization is valid
questions.stem: Ben takes a random sample of 50 students and finds that 30 prefer apples. Cara takes a random sample of 50 students from the same school and finds that 28 prefer apples. Which is the most reasonable conclusion?
choices: A little over half of the school probably prefers apples
Ben's sample is wrong because it differs from Cara's sample
Exactly 29 of every 50 students at the school prefer apples
Nothing can be learned from either of the two samples
questions.answer: A little over half of the school probably prefers apples
questions.solution: Two random samples from the same population can differ a little. Both show a bit more than half prefer apples, so that is a reasonable conclusion. They do not prove an exact count.

solve.answer: A little over half of the school probably prefers apples
solve.work: Ben 60%, Cara 56%; samples vary naturally; both suggest a little over half prefer apples.

questions.skill: Use a sample to estimate for the population
questions.stem: In a random sample, 12 of 30 students said they like chess. Using the sample, the school predicts that 240 of its students like chess. How many students does the school have?
questions.solution: 12 out of 30 is $\frac{2}{5}$. If $\frac{2}{5}$ of the school is 240 students, the school has $240 \div \frac{2}{5} = 600$ students.

questions.skill: Tell the population from the sample
questions.stem: A district has 4 schools with 320, 410, 275 and 395 students. A survey is meant to describe all the students in the district. How many students are in the population?
questions.solution: The population is all the students in all 4 schools: $320 + 410 + 275 + 395 = 1400$.

solve.work: 320+410+275+395 = 1400; the population is all district students.

questions.skill: Choose a random, representative sampling method
questions.stem: Which of these does NOT give every student in a school an equal chance of being chosen?
choices: Drawing 40 names from a bag after mixing all the names
Using a computer to pick 40 student ID numbers at random
Asking for volunteers who raise their hands
Shuffling a card for every student and drawing 40 cards
questions.answer: Asking for volunteers who raise their hands
questions.solution: With volunteers, only students who choose to raise their hands can be in the sample. The other methods give every student the same chance.

solve.answer: Asking for volunteers who raise their hands
solve.work: Volunteers self-select, so not every student has an equal chance; the other three are random.

questions.skill: Choose a random, representative sampling method
questions.stem: A mall wants a representative sample of all the people who visit it. Which plan is best?
choices: Ask the 100 people sitting in the food court on Saturday at noon
Ask 100 people who are shopping inside one single store
Ask the 100 shoppers who are carrying the biggest shopping bags
Ask random visitors on different days and at different times
questions.answer: Ask random visitors on different days and at different times
questions.solution: Visitors differ by day, time and store. A plan that spreads random choices over different days and times covers all kinds of visitors. The other plans reach only one kind of shopper.

solve.answer: Ask random visitors on different days and at different times
solve.work: Random visitors across different days and times represent all visitors; the others are restricted groups.

questions.skill: Spot why a sample is biased
questions.stem: At a school chess tournament, 18 of the 20 students surveyed say they like chess. A student concludes that 90 percent of the whole school likes chess. What is the main flaw?
choices: Twenty students is too many students for a sample
Tournament players are not typical of the school
18 out of 20 students is not the same as 90 percent
Students at a tournament never answer questions honestly
questions.answer: Tournament players are not typical of the school
questions.solution: 18 out of 20 really is 90 percent, so the arithmetic is fine. The flaw is the sample: students at a chess tournament are more likely to like chess than the rest of the school.

solve.answer: Tournament players are not typical of the school
solve.work: 18/20 = 90% is correct arithmetic; the flaw is that tournament players are not typical of the school.

questions.skill: Spot why a sample is biased
questions.stem: A manager emails a survey to all 400 employees. Only 30 reply, and most are upset. Why can't the results be trusted for all employees?
choices: Employees who replied chose themselves, unlike the rest
Surveys sent by email to employees are never allowed
A survey needs exactly half of the group to send a reply
Thirty replies are more than the whole company has staff
questions.answer: Employees who replied chose themselves, unlike the rest
questions.solution: The 30 who replied picked themselves, and people who are upset are often more likely to reply. They may not represent the other 370 employees.

solve.answer: Employees who replied chose themselves, unlike the rest
solve.work: The 30 who replied chose to reply (voluntary response), so may differ from the rest.

questions.skill: Judge whether a generalization is valid
questions.stem: In a random sample of 120 shoppers at a mall, 90 have a coupon. Which statement is best supported?
choices: About three-fourths of the shoppers at every mall have a coupon
Exactly 90 of all the shoppers at this mall have a coupon
About three-fourths of the shoppers here probably have a coupon
Every one of the shoppers at this mall has a coupon
questions.answer: About three-fourths of the shoppers here probably have a coupon
questions.solution: 90 out of 120 is three-fourths. The sample was taken at this mall, so it supports a statement about this mall only, and only as an estimate, not an exact count or a claim about every shopper.

solve.answer: About three-fourths of the shoppers here probably have a coupon
solve.work: 90/120 = 3/4; random sample of this mall's shoppers supports 'about three-fourths here probably'; not every mall.

questions.skill: Judge whether a generalization is valid
questions.stem: Tia picks 3 students at random from her school and all 3 like math. She says that all students at the school like math. Is her conclusion valid?
choices: Yes, because the 3 students were picked by a fair random draw
Yes, because all 3 of the students gave the same answer
No, because random samples can never be reliable at all
No, because 3 students are too few to speak for everyone
questions.answer: No, because 3 students are too few to speak for everyone
questions.solution: Random picking is good, but 3 students is a very small sample and could easily be far from the whole school. A small sample cannot support a claim about everyone.

solve.answer: No, because 3 students are too few to speak for everyone
solve.work: A sample of 3 is too small to conclude that ALL students like math; random draws can still be unrepresentative when tiny.

questions.skill: Estimate a population count from a random sample
questions.stem: A factory tests a random sample of 200 light bulbs and finds that 6 are defective. About how many defective bulbs would you expect in a batch of 5,000 bulbs?
questions.solution: 6 out of 200 is 3%. Three percent of 5,000 is 150 bulbs.

questions.skill: Compare estimates from several random samples
questions.stem: Five random samples each gave an estimate of the percent of students who like art: 40, 44, 38, 42 and 46. What is the range of these five estimates, in percentage points?
questions.solution: The largest estimate is 46 and the smallest is 38, so the range is 46 - 38 = 8.

questions.skill: Combine several random samples into one estimate
questions.stem: Three random samples of 25 students each found 10, 12 and 14 students who prefer apples. What is the mean number of students per sample who prefer apples?
questions.solution: The sum is 10 + 12 + 14 = 36. The mean is 36 / 3 = 12 students.

questions.skill: Estimate a population count from a random sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 40 students from a school of 600 students found that 10 of the 40 prefer soccer. Based on the sample, estimate how many of the 600 students prefer soccer.
questions.solution: 10 out of 40 is 1/4 of the sample. One fourth of 600 is 150 students.

questions.skill: Explain why random samples give different results
questions.stem: Two random samples of 30 students each are taken from one school. They find 12 and 15 students who ride the bus. Why do the results differ?
choices: One of the samples must have been counted wrongly by someone
The number of bus riders at the school changed between the samples
Random samples from one school must always give the same result
Each sample has different students, so the results vary by chance
questions.answer: Each sample has different students, so the results vary by chance
questions.solution: Each random sample picks different students, so counts differ a little from sample to sample. This is normal variation, not a mistake.

solve.answer: Each sample has different students, so the results vary by chance
solve.work: Random samples contain different students, so counts vary by chance (sampling variability).

questions.skill: Sample size and variation in estimates
questions.stem: Mia asks random students how many pets they have, using a sample of 15 students or a sample of 150 students. She could repeat either sample many times. Which sample would give estimates that vary less?
choices: Both would vary by the same amount
Neither; random samples always give the same value
questions.solution: Larger random samples give estimates that are closer together from sample to sample.

questions.skill: Estimate a population percent from a random sample
questions.stem: In a random sample of 80 library visitors, 20 borrowed a book. Which is the best estimate of the percent of all visitors who borrow a book?
questions.solution: 20 out of 80 is 1/4, which is 25%.

questions.skill: Estimate a population mean or total from a sample mean
questions.stem: A random sample of 5 students were asked how many books they read last month. The answers were 6, 8, 7, 9 and 10. Use the sample mean to estimate the mean number of books read by all students in the school.
questions.solution: The sum is 6 + 8 + 7 + 9 + 10 = 40. The mean is 40 / 5 = 8 books.

questions.skill: Judge a claim using several random samples
questions.stem: A random sample of 50 students found that 20 own a bike. A school has 500 students. A student says about 200 of them own a bike. Which statement is best?
choices: This is not reasonable: a sample can never predict a whole school
This is not reasonable: the answer should be 20, the sample count
This is reasonable: 20 out of 50 is 40%, and 40% of 500 is 200
This is not reasonable: 500 divided by 50 is 10, so about 10 students
questions.answer: This is reasonable: 20 out of 50 is 40%, and 40% of 500 is 200
questions.solution: 20 out of 50 is 40%. If the sample is typical, 40% of the 500 students is 200 students.

solve.answer: This is reasonable: 20 out of 50 is 40%, and 40% of 500 is 200

questions.skill: Compare estimates from several random samples
questions.stem: Four random samples of the same size gave estimates of 30%, 32%, 34% and 32% for the percent of students who walk to school. Which statement is best?
choices: The estimates are different, so none of them can be trusted
The percent in the school must be exactly equal to 30%
The percent in the school must be exactly equal to 34%
The estimates are close, so the percent is probably near 32%
questions.answer: The estimates are close, so the percent is probably near 32%
questions.solution: The four estimates are close and their mean is 32%, so about 32% of all students probably walk.

solve.answer: The estimates are close, so the percent is probably near 32%
solve.work: Estimates vary slightly around 32%; the best inference is the percent is probably near 32%.

questions.skill: Compare estimates from several random samples
questions.stem: Ravi takes five random samples of the same size and finds the proportion of left-handed students: 0.08, 0.12, 0.10, 0.11 and 0.09. Which is the best estimate of the proportion of left-handed students in the whole school?
questions.solution: The mean of the five proportions is 0.50 / 5 = 0.10, so about 0.10 of the students are left-handed.

questions.skill: Sample size and variation in estimates
questions.stem: Sam took many random samples of size 10 and his estimates ranged from 20% to 80%. Tia took many random samples of size 100 from the same population and her estimates ranged from 45% to 55%. Which conclusion is best?
choices: Larger samples vary less, so Tia's estimates are more dependable
Smaller samples are more dependable because they are easier to count
The ranges differ because Sam and Tia sampled different populations
The range of the estimates does not depend on the sample size
questions.answer: Larger samples vary less, so Tia's estimates are more dependable
questions.solution: Tia's larger samples gave a much narrower range, which shows that larger random samples vary less.

solve.answer: Larger samples vary less, so Tia's estimates are more dependable
solve.work: Larger samples give estimates with less variability, so Tia's are more dependable.

questions.skill: Combine several random samples into one estimate
questions.stem: Six random samples of the same size were used to find the mean number of text messages sent per day. The sample means were 12, 15, 11, 14, 13 and 13. Estimate the population mean by finding the mean of these sample means.
questions.solution: The sum is 12 + 15 + 11 + 14 + 13 + 13 = 78. The mean is 78 / 6 = 13 messages.

questions.skill: Compare estimates from several random samples
questions.stem: Seven random samples gave these estimates of the percent of students who own a pet: 47, 42, 50, 45, 41, 44 and 46. Use the median of the seven estimates as the estimate of the percent of all students who own a pet.
questions.solution: In order the estimates are 41, 42, 44, 45, 46, 47, 50. The middle value is 45, so the estimate is 45%.

questions.skill: Explain why random samples give different results
questions.stem: Nina takes a random sample of 30 students and finds that 18 prefer red. She says that exactly 60% of all students in the school prefer red. What is wrong with her statement?
choices: Nothing is wrong, because a random sample shows the exact percent of all students
A new random sample could give a different percent, so 60% is an estimate
A percent cannot be found from a sample of only 30 students at all
The percent should be found by adding 18 and 30 and then halving it
questions.answer: A new random sample could give a different percent, so 60% is an estimate
questions.solution: A sample gives an estimate. A different random sample would probably give a slightly different percent.

solve.answer: A new random sample could give a different percent, so 60% is an estimate
solve.work: 18/30 = 60% is a sample estimate; another random sample would vary, so it is not exact.

questions.skill: Combine several random samples into one estimate
questions.stem: Four random samples of 50 students each found that 21, 24, 18 and 25 students walk to school. Use all four samples together to estimate how many of the 1,200 students in the school walk to school.
questions.solution: In all, 21 + 24 + 18 + 25 = 88 of the 200 students sampled walk. That is 44%, and 44% of 1,200 is 528.

questions.skill: Sample size and variation in estimates
questions.stem: Lina takes random samples of the same size to estimate a mean, and her estimates vary a lot. What could she do to make the estimates vary less?
choices: Use a smaller random sample each time
Ask only students she knows well
Use a larger random sample each time
Ask the same student again and again
questions.answer: Use a larger random sample each time
questions.solution: Larger random samples vary less. Asking only friends, or the same student, would not be a random sample.

solve.answer: Use a larger random sample each time

questions.skill: Judge a claim using several random samples
questions.stem: A company says that 90% of its customers are satisfied. Three random samples of 50 customers had 36, 35 and 37 satisfied customers. Which statement is best?
choices: The claim is supported: more than half of each sample is satisfied
The claim is supported: samples vary, so any percent is possible
The claim is supported: the counts 36, 35 and 37 are close to each other
The claim is doubtful: all three samples are near 70%, far below 90%
questions.answer: The claim is doubtful: all three samples are near 70%, far below 90%
questions.solution: 36, 35 and 37 out of 50 are 72%, 70% and 74%. These are close together and far from 90%, so the claim is doubtful.

solve.answer: The claim is doubtful: all three samples are near 70%, far below 90%

questions.skill: Estimate a population count from a random sample
questions.stem: A random sample suggests that 3/8 of the students in a school play an instrument. About 270 students at the school play an instrument. Based on this estimate, how many students attend the school?
questions.solution: 3/8 of the students is 270, so 1/8 is 270 / 3 = 90. All 8 eighths are 8 x 90 = 720 students.

questions.skill: Estimate a population mean or total from a sample mean
questions.stem: A cafe has 400 receipts. A random sample of 8 receipts had totals of 6, 9, 12, 7, 10, 8, 11 and 9 dollars. Use the sample mean to estimate the total of all 400 receipts, in dollars.
questions.solution: The sum of the sample is 72, so the sample mean is 72 / 8 = 9 dollars. For 400 receipts the estimate is 9 x 400 = 3,600 dollars.

questions.skill: Judge a claim using several random samples
questions.stem: A town says its mean commute is 25 minutes. Six random samples of 40 residents gave sample means of 24, 27, 25, 26, 23 and 25 minutes. Which statement is best?
choices: The claim is plausible: the sample means cluster around 25 minutes
The claim is false: only two of the sample means are equal to 25
The claim is false: the sample means are not all the same number
The claim is false: the largest sample mean is 27, which is above 25
questions.answer: The claim is plausible: the sample means cluster around 25 minutes
questions.solution: The sample means are 24, 27, 25, 26, 23 and 25, and their mean is 150 / 6 = 25 minutes. Random samples vary, and these vary only a little around 25, so the claim is plausible.

solve.answer: The claim is plausible: the sample means cluster around 25 minutes
solve.work: Sample means 23-27 cluster around 25; variation is expected, so the claim is plausible.

questions.skill: Combine several random samples into one estimate
questions.stem: A random sample of 80 items had 5 defective items, and another random sample of 120 items had 9 defective items. Treat the two samples as one combined sample. Estimate how many defective items are in a shipment of 4,000 items.
questions.solution: In all, 14 of the 200 sampled items are defective, which is 7%. Seven percent of 4,000 is 280 items.

questions.skill: Estimate a population count from a random sample
questions.stem: Six random samples of 40 students each found 4, 5, 3, 6, 4 and 5 left-handed students. Which is the best estimate of the number of left-handed students in a school of 900?
questions.solution: In all, 27 of the 240 students sampled are left-handed. That is 11.25%, and 11.25% of 900 is about 100.

questions.skill: Combine several random samples into one estimate
questions.stem: A bag holds 200 marbles, some blue. A student mixes the bag, draws 20 marbles at random, records the number of blue ones, and puts them back. Over 10 draws the blue counts were 6, 8, 7, 9, 5, 7, 8, 6, 7 and 7. Estimate how many of the 200 marbles are blue.
questions.solution: In all, 70 blue marbles were drawn out of 10 x 20 = 200 marbles. That is 35%, and 35% of 200 is 70.

solve.work: Sum of counts = 70; mean 7 blue per 20. 7/20 * 200 = 70.

questions.skill: Sample size and variation in estimates
questions.stem: One class takes 50 random samples of size 20, and another class takes 50 random samples of size 200, all from the same population. Which description of the 100 estimates is most likely?
choices: The estimates from size 20 are more tightly clustered than those from size 200
The estimates from size 200 are more tightly clustered than those from size 20
The two groups of estimates are spread out by the same amount as each other
All the estimates from size 200 are exactly equal to the population value
questions.answer: The estimates from size 200 are more tightly clustered than those from size 20
questions.solution: Larger random samples vary less, so the estimates from size 200 are closer together.

solve.answer: The estimates from size 200 are more tightly clustered than those from size 20
solve.work: Larger samples give less variable estimates, so size-200 estimates cluster more tightly.

questions.skill: Compare estimates from several random samples
questions.stem: Five random samples gave estimates of 12%, 18%, 15%, 14% and 16% for the percent of students who use a library card. Which statement is best supported?
choices: The percent for all students is exactly 15%, the mean of the estimates
The percent for all students is probably above 18%, the largest estimate
The percent for all students is probably between 12% and 18%, near 15%
The estimates differ, so sampling cannot give useful information
questions.answer: The percent for all students is probably between 12% and 18%, near 15%
questions.solution: The five estimates run from 12% to 18% and their mean is 75 / 5 = 15%. They suggest a value near 15%, not an exact one.

solve.answer: The percent for all students is probably between 12% and 18%, near 15%
solve.work: Estimates vary around 15% within 12-18%; best supported: probably between 12% and 18%, near 15%.

questions.skill: Estimate a population count from a random sample
questions.stem: Biologists tag 50 fish in a lake and release them. Later they catch a random sample of 40 fish and find that 5 have tags. Assuming the sample is typical, estimate how many fish are in the lake.
questions.solution: 5 of the 40 sampled fish, or 1/8, are tagged. The 50 tagged fish are about 1/8 of all the fish, so there are about 50 x 8 = 400 fish.

questions.skill: Estimate a population count from a random sample
questions.stem: In a random sample of 150 residents, 63 said they favor a new park. About how many of the 9,000 residents of the town would be expected to favor the new park?
questions.solution: 63 out of 150 is 0.42. Then 0.42 x 9,000 = 3,780 residents.

questions.skill: Compare estimates from several random samples
questions.stem: Four students each took five random samples of the same size from one population. Which list of the five sample proportions has the smallest range?
questions.solution: The ranges are 0.04, 0.12, 0.22 and 0.12. The list 0.40 to 0.44 has the smallest range.

questions.skill: Estimate a population mean or total from a sample mean
questions.stem: A random sample of 10 students reported their daily screen time in hours: 2, 3, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 3, 2 and 3. Use the sample mean to estimate the total daily screen time, in hours, of all 250 students in the grade.
questions.solution: The sum of the sample is 28 hours, so the mean is 2.8 hours. For 250 students the estimate is 2.8 x 250 = 700 hours.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: The high temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit, on 7 days in Town A were 62, 65, 68, 64, 70, 66, 67. What is the range of these temperatures?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value. The greatest is 70 and the least is 62, so the range is $70 - 62 = 8$ degrees.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Four friends read 3, 5, 7 and 9 pages of a book. The mean is 6 pages. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the numbers of pages?
questions.solution: Find how far each value is from the mean 6: 3, 1, 1 and 3. The mean of these distances is $(3 + 1 + 1 + 3) \div 4 = 2$ pages.

questions.skill: Compare the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: The mean absolute deviation (MAD) of Class A's quiz scores is 2.1. The MAD of Class B's quiz scores is 4.6. Which statement is true?
choices: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
Class A's scores are more spread out than Class B's
Class A's scores are higher than Class B's
Class B's scores are higher than Class A's
questions.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
questions.solution: The MAD tells how far values typically are from their mean. A larger MAD means the values are more spread out. Class B's MAD, 4.6, is larger than Class A's, 2.1, so Class B's scores are more spread out. The MAD says nothing about which class scored higher.

solve.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
solve.work: Larger MAD means more spread; MAD says nothing about which is higher.

questions.skill: Express the difference between centers as a multiple of the variability

questions.skill: Interpret a measure of variability

The mean of the data set is a small number
There are only a few values in the data set
The values are close to the mean on average

questions.solution: The MAD is the average distance of the values from the mean. A small MAD means the values are, on average, close to the mean. It says nothing about how large the mean is or how many values there are.

solve.work: MAD is average distance from mean; small means values are close to the mean.

Sample B varies more: its MAD is 4, while Sample A's MAD is 1.
